items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: That’s Ernst Konitz or Ernst Toch — Toch was before Ernst Konitz.

ctx.x: Yeah. Most of the jazz players get into this, all the G 7th to C flat 9 and the flat 5 and all of that, doing it that way. But I’ve always thought, ever since I’ve studied, and I studied extensively with three or four fine teachers, different styles and I found that all of them think of the linear way to go, the lines are the strongest force in music. In that if you have a line and it’s strong enough it doesn’t matter what happens below. If you have two lines going here and you try to analyze what’s happening at…
